data.overview: Payload Preview (PRD F-6) is the Payload tab's three-section readout — Prompt, Crops, Hierarchy — plus a footer summary, letting a reporter see exactly what MCP/Claude Code will receive before sending. It is pure assembly over data two completed specs already produce: F-4 (drag-annotate-frozen-frame)'s StagedAnnotation list and F-5 (measure-mode)'s cached HierarchySnapshotModel and finding-carrying annotation comments. Android-hosted, Desktop-rendered (presentation-feature-mirror); no new platform surface.
data.problemStatement: The reporter currently has no way to see the actual bundle (prompt text, cropped evidence images, hierarchy tree, size) before it is sent to the agent — trust in the one-shot handoff requires inspecting and lightly tuning what gets sent, not sending blind.
data.purpose: Render the Payload tab's Prompt/Crops/Hierarchy sections and footer from data F-4 and F-5 already produce, so the reporter can verify and (minimally) tune the exact payload before Resolve & Send.
goals: Assemble the prompt, token estimate, crop grid and hierarchy tree from already-shipped state (StagedAnnotation, HierarchySnapshotModel, DeviceModel) with zero new data sources.
Keep the token estimate and payload size formulas honest heuristics that visibly match what is actually attached, never drifting from the real send.
Degrade clearly, not silently, when zero annotations are staged or the hierarchy dump produced nothing usable (HierarchyStatus.Unavailable).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given at least one staged annotation exists, when the user opens the Payload tab, then a generated text prompt with token-count estimate and an Edit affordance is shown.
Given staged annotations exist, when viewing Payload > Crops, then a 3-column grid shows each annotation's cropped image with its red outline baked in and caption 'from frame <id>'.
Given staged annotations exist, when viewing Payload > Hierarchy, then a monospace indented tree displays with matched/flagged nodes visually marked.
Given the Payload tab is open, then its footer summarizes 'frame.png · N crops · hierarchy.xml' plus a total size that matches the actual payload.

Crop captions and any pixel dimensions in the Payload tab render with the unspaced × (U+00D7) multiplication sign, reusing AnnotationFormat.kt's metaLine pattern — never a letter x and never a new formatter.

The per-annotation prompt line is built from StagedAnnotation.rect and StagedAnnotation.comment verbatim (which already carries any ⌥-prefixed measurement line from measure-mode's noteLine/replaceNoteLine) with no separate 'measured:' branch, regardless of whether the user ever held Option on that annotation.
The Hierarchy section's source label reads 'uiautomator · {nodes.size} nodes' from the already-cached HierarchySnapshotModel (MirrorViewModel.frozenHierarchy); it never triggers a new dump.

A hierarchy node is marked (red '#{annotationIndex}' badge, ink color) if and only if it is the result of NodeSnap.snapTarget for that annotation's rect; every other node renders in ink3 with no badge.
The crop red outline is positioned using exactly crop(annotationRect, 84, 72, 14, fixed=false, withRect=true)'s returned rect — never a differently-padded or unscaled rect.

Given zero staged annotations, the Payload tab renders only the literal empty-state copy ('Nothing staged. Draw a box and the payload builds here, exactly as Claude will get it.') — none of Prompt, Crops, Hierarchy or the footer render.

Token estimate (360 + count*140) and payload size ((1.6 + count*0.12) MB, one decimal) recompute synchronously as annotations are added/removed/edited, with no measurable lag (satisfies NFR-11's ~200ms budget trivially since both are O(1) arithmetic).

Clicking the Edit affordance toggles the prompt block into an editable text area (reusing the existing MultilineInput atom); the edited text, once changed, is what gets attached as the prompt instead of the auto-generated text.

When HierarchyStatus is Unavailable or Absent for the frozen frame, the Hierarchy section shows zero nodes and an explicit 'no hierarchy' state rather than an empty tree that looks like a bug, and the rest of the Payload tab (Prompt, Crops, footer) still renders normally.

functionalRequirements.text: In the Payload tab's Prompt section, show the auto-generated text prompt, its token-count estimate, and an Edit affordance.
In the Payload tab's Crops section, show a 3-column grid of per-annotation cropped images with the red outline baked in, each captioned 'from frame <id>'.
In the Payload tab's Hierarchy section, show a monospace, indented view-hierarchy tree with matched/flagged nodes visually marked.
Show a Payload footer summarizing contents ('frame.png · N crops · hierarchy.xml') and total payload size.

Prompt assembly builds one line per staged annotation from its rect (metaLine-style) plus its comment verbatim — comment already carries any ⌥-prefixed measurement line from measure-mode, so no separate finding branch exists.
Token estimate = 360 + (staged annotation count × 140); recomputed whenever the annotation count changes, with no tokenizer dependency.

For each staged annotation, compute crop(rect, bw=84, bh=72, pad=14, fixed=false, withRect=true) and render the cropped frame slice with the baked red outline plus caption '#{index}·{w}×{h}' using the annotation rect's own raw pixel dimensions.

Hierarchy section renders HierarchySnapshotModel.nodes as indented rows (indent = node.depth) labeled 'uiautomator · {nodes.size} nodes'; a node returned by NodeSnap.snapTarget for any staged annotation gets a red '#{annotationIndex}' badge and ink color, every other node is ink3.
Footer renders 'frame.png · {count} crops · hierarchy.xml' (left) and '{(1.6 + count*0.12).toFixed(1)} MB' (right); Payload tab only.

The prompt's device/resolution line reads the real selected device (DeviceModel.displayName + DeviceModel.androidVersion) and the real frozen frame size (FrozenFrame.deviceSize) — never the design's hardcoded 'Pixel 8 Pro · Android 15 · 1344×2992' literal.

Edit affordance click toggles the prompt block between read-only mono text and an editable MultilineInput; the edited text, once non-empty and changed, overrides the auto-generated prompt for sending.
When zero annotations are staged, the Payload tab renders only the empty-state copy; Prompt, Crops, Hierarchy and the footer do not render at all (matches the design's own count === 0 gate).
Crops section header shows 'from frame {frameId}' where frameId is a new per-session sequential freeze counter (increments once per freeze), not a device timestamp or literal placeholder.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Token-count estimation for the generated prompt computes without perceptible delay (target under ~200ms) before Resolve & Send is enabled.
The payload format (prompt + crops + hierarchy XML) is versioned so the receiving MCP server/Claude Code agent can evolve its parsing without breaking older sends.

outOfScope: iOS payload preview — no view-hierarchy-dump equivalent exists for iOS in this codebase (same boundary as measure-mode's AS-19); ios-platform-support is a separate backlog item.
Real tokenizer integration — ships the design's 360+count*140 heuristic; a genuine tokenizer dependency is a future upgrade only if the heuristic proves materially wrong.
A new Compose UI-test harness — visual/geometry acceptance criteria (AC-67-style, AC-80) stay manual (demo), consistent with testing.md and measure-mode's precedent.

Mirroring the payload footer into the Notes tab (unless the survey answer below picks that option) — SidePanelFrame's content slot is per-tab with no shared footer, so this is additive scope, not a given.
New HierarchyStatus states or hierarchy phase visuals beyond dumping/ready/sent/unavailable — reuses the enum measure-mode already shipped, no new states invented here.

constraints.text: Android only: the hierarchy dump source (HierarchySnapshotModel) has no iOS equivalent in this codebase; payload-preview inherits measure-mode's Android-only boundary.

No new dependency for tokenization or hierarchy parsing — reuse NodeSnap.snapTarget, AnnotationFormat.TIMES/metaLine, MeasureFormat's noteLine shape, and HierarchySnapshotModel/HierarchyStatus as already shipped.

All colors/typography must come from Theme.* tokens: RED→Theme.color.annotate, OK→Theme.color.sentFixed, WARN→Theme.color.warnStillOff (verified in ThemeColor.kt), plus ink/ink2/ink3/codeBg/line — no new tokens expected.
SidePanelFrame's content lambda is per-tab with no shared footer slot; a Notes-tab-mirrored footer (if chosen) must be added directly to MirrorNotesTab, not the SidePanelFrame organism.

assumptions.text: The view hierarchy is already dumped once at freeze time and cached (measure-mode's AS-18): HierarchySnapshotModel lives on MirrorViewModel.frozenHierarchy, its readiness mirrored via MirrorUiState.hierarchyStatus (HierarchyStatus.Absent/Dumping/Ready/Unavailable). Payload-preview reads this cache only and never triggers its own dump — this resolves input ambiguity #4 (hierarchy source & timing) from measure-mode's already-shipped decision rather than re-surveying it.
Payload-preview ships Android-only, matching measure-mode's AS-19; iOS has no hierarchy-dump equivalent wired and stays out of scope.

The design's WARN/OK/RED constants map to Theme.color.warnStillOff / Theme.color.sentFixed / Theme.color.annotate respectively (verified by reading ThemeColor.kt's doc comments) — no new color tokens are needed.

Crop caption and any other raw-pixel dimension text reuses the existing unspaced × (U+00D7) pattern from AnnotationFormat.kt's metaLine rather than inventing a new 'D()' formatter — this resolves input ambiguity #8.

Measure-mode already folds any measurement finding into StagedAnnotation.comment (⌥-prefixed line via noteLine/replaceNoteLine); the prompt's per-annotation text is therefore the comment verbatim with no parallel finding field to check — this resolves input ambiguity #5 without a special-case branch.

Frame id, the Edit affordance's depth, and the token formula's finality are the three decisions genuinely not resolvable from existing code or design text; the proposedSurvey below carries the recommended defaults until the orchestrator's survey returns user edits.

dependencies.note: Supplies StagedAnnotation (rect, comment, index) and FrozenFrame (deviceSize) that the prompt, crops and footer are built from.

Supplies the cached HierarchySnapshotModel/HierarchyStatus the Hierarchy section reads, the NodeSnap.snapTarget function reused for badge matching, and the ⌥-prefixed finding lines already folded into annotation comments.

scenarios.title: Review payload before sending
steps: Open Payload tab
Review generated prompt and token estimate
Review crops grid
Review hierarchy tree
Check footer summary

scenarios.title: Payload with zero staged annotations
steps: Freeze a frame with no annotations drawn
Open the Payload tab
Only the empty-state copy renders
No Prompt/Crops/Hierarchy section or footer appears

scenarios.title: Annotation with no matched hierarchy node
steps: Stage an annotation whose rect contains no hierarchy node within NodeSnap's slack
Open Payload > Hierarchy
No node carries that annotation's badge
Open Payload > Crops: the crop still renders using the annotation's own rect for the outline

scenarios.title: Prompt assembles correctly without any measurement
steps: Stage annotations without ever holding Option over any of them
Open Payload > Prompt
Each annotation line shows its comment (or 'no comment') with no finding text, and the prompt is otherwise well-formed

scenarios.title: Freeze-time hierarchy dump was unavailable
steps: Freeze a frame whose uiautomator dump failed or returned empty (HierarchyStatus.Unavailable)
Open Payload > Hierarchy
Section shows zero nodes with an explicit 'no hierarchy' state, not a silent empty tree
Prompt, Crops and the footer still render normally

scenarios.title: Edit the prompt before sending
steps: Open Payload tab with staged annotations
Click the Edit affordance
Prompt block becomes an editable text area
Edited text becomes the prompt that would be attached to the send

successMetrics: Token estimate and payload size shown in the UI always match what is actually assembled for the send — no displayed-vs-real drift.
Every annotation's crop, caption and hierarchy badge stay index-consistent with the Notes tab list across edits/deletes.
openQuestions: Should an edited prompt override auto-clear when annotations subsequently change, or persist until the user clicks Edit again? Default assumed: persists until Edit is clicked again (no auto-clear) — simplest, no silent data loss.
Real tokenizer integration remains a candidate future upgrade over the heuristic formula if it proves materially misleading at scale; not pursued in this spec.
Where the new per-session freeze counter (FR-55) is hosted (FrozenFrame vs. MirrorViewModel) is left to Stage 2 planning.

proposedSurvey.question: Crops section header shows 'from frame {frameId}' — where does frameId come from? (No frame id field exists anywhere in the codebase today; this mints one.)
options: New per-session sequential freeze counter (increments by 1 each time the stage freezes; simplest new field, no clock dependency)
Device-timestamp-based id (epoch millis at freeze time; requires reading the device/system clock at freeze)
Drop the label entirely for v1 (Crops header shows just 'CROPS', no 'from frame <id>' caption)
proposedSurvey.recommended: New per-session sequential freeze counter (increments by 1 each time the stage freezes; simplest new field, no clock dependency)
proposedSurvey.rationale: Neither FrozenFrame nor StagedAnnotation carries any id or timestamp today, so every option mints a new field. A sequential counter is the smallest addition (one Int, no clock/platform dependency) and is deterministic for tests, unlike a wall-clock timestamp.

proposedSurvey.question: What does clicking the Prompt section's 'Edit' affordance do?
options: Toggle the prompt block into an editable text area (reuse the existing MultilineInput atom); edited text becomes the prompt actually sent
Copy-to-clipboard only — no editing capability, button just copies the generated text
Render the affordance but leave it disabled/inert for v1 — satisfies FR-12's 'shown' requirement via inspection only, no behavior yet
proposedSurvey.recommended: Toggle the prompt block into an editable text area (reuse the existing MultilineInput atom); edited text becomes the prompt actually sent
proposedSurvey.rationale: presentation-core-ui already ships MultilineInput (120-240dp scrollable text atom) with zero new component work, and US-6's stated reason for this feature is letting the reporter 'trust and tune' the payload — a disabled or copy-only Edit button satisfies the letter of FR-12 but not the feature's own purpose.

proposedSurvey.question: Does the token-count estimate ship as the design's heuristic formula (360 + count*140), or integrate a real tokenizer?
options: Ship the heuristic formula as the real, final estimate — O(1) arithmetic, trivially meets NFR-11's ~200ms budget, no new dependency
Integrate a genuine tokenizer library against the prompt text for an accurate count
proposedSurvey.recommended: Ship the heuristic formula as the real, final estimate — O(1) arithmetic, trivially meets NFR-11's ~200ms budget, no new dependency
proposedSurvey.rationale: No tokenizer dependency exists in the version catalog today, and the design explicitly specifies this formula as final, not a placeholder. Adding a tokenizer is a real dependency decision nothing in the input asks for; the heuristic is honest about being an estimate ('≈ {tokens} tokens').

proposedSurvey.question: Does the payload footer (frame.png · N crops · hierarchy.xml · size) appear only in the Payload tab, or also mirrored into the Notes tab footer?
options: Payload tab only — matches the design screenshot literally, zero changes to MirrorNotesTab
Both tabs — add the same summary row to MirrorNotesTab as well, duplicating it
proposedSurvey.recommended: Payload tab only — matches the design screenshot literally, zero changes to MirrorNotesTab
proposedSurvey.rationale: The design's own screenshot only shows this footer under the Payload tab; SidePanelFrame's content slot is per-tab with no shared footer mechanism today, so mirroring it into Notes is additive scope nothing in the input requires.
